This translation cannot be called original; Because he created some extra-Shakespearean characters and added a new scene at the end of the play called 'organ'.  (Page: 45)

As he 'Indianized' the names of the characters in this drama written in prose and verse, he also made several changes in the mood and language to improve the structure of the composition. Even so, 'the book is a total failure as a drama and totally worthless as a text. However, it must be admitted that Harchandra did not write the book as a play, but as a textbook. His hope was that the book would be appreciated as a textbook for its composition-system and story-glory'.  Revere and Long wrote about this play that: ... Shakespeare's ideas, but given in a Bengali dress, well and ably done'.

For example: 'I ... undertook to write in the shape of a Bengali Natak or drama taking only the plot and sub plots of The Merchant of Venice with considerable additions and alterations to suit the native test.' Commodity-authored books are not the only recent passion of universities.’ (Page: 46)

Harachandra in his translation gives the Indian name of Shylock as 'Lakshapati', and of Porcia as 'Bhanumati'. import numpy as np
from keras.models import Sequential
from keras.layers import LSTM, Dense

# Read and preprocess the dataset
def read_dataset(file_path):
    with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
        lines = file.read().split("\n")

    chars = sorted(list(set(text)))
    char_to_idx = {char: idx for idx, char in enumerate(chars)}
    idx_to_char = {idx: char for idx, char in enumerate(chars)}
    
    return text, chars, char_to_idx, idx_to_char

    sequences = []
    targets = []
    for i in range(len(text) - seq_length):
        sequence = text[i:i+seq_length]
        target = text[i+seq_length]
        sequences.append([char_to_idx[char] for char in sequence])
        targets.append(char_to_idx[target])

    return np.array(sequences), np.array(targets)

The opening episode of House of the Dragon (Sky Atlantic) is simply spectacular. For an hour, it rattles through everything that made its predecessor, Game of Thrones, such a titan of the small screen, especially when it was in its prime. It is a greatest hits playlist of Westeros at its meatiest. Family members make promises they cannot keep as they connive and betray each other, in secret and in plain sight. There is jousting, romping and fighting. There are dragons, of course. There is a drunken orgy, an axe to the face, a caesarean without anaesthetic, seeping wounds, severed limbs and severed organs, too. George RR Martin’s world struts its way back on to our screens with utter confidence and brio.

It is as captivating as it is gruesome. A prequel to Game of Thrones, it begins 172 years before the birth of Daenerys Targaryen, and it chronicles the fall of the Targaryen dynasty, though after watching the first six episodes of squabbling and scheming, the real question is how it can possibly take two centuries to collapse. It opens with the Lear-esque prospect of a failing king choosing his heir, and though the people shift slightly over the course of the series, succession is the thread that keeps it all together.


Episodes one to five centre on young Princess Rhaenyra (played by Milly Alcock), the only child of King Viserys I (Paddy Considine). Rhaenyra is a strong, ambitious and courageous teenage girl, and would be an ideal heir, were it not for the fact that the Lords have already made it clear, in very recent history, that tradition demands a king, and not a queen, on the Iron Throne. In this world, royal women are breeding machines and bargaining chips. “I am glad I am not a woman,” says one male character, later in the series. It could be the tagline for the whole thing.

Amid much grumbling about Rhaenyra, Viserys’s brother steps forward. Daemon is a hotheaded peacock who refuses to play by any rules he considers beneath him. The political wheel turns on a rumour, and as Viserys begins to appear frail, there is a growing sense of urgency about where the wheel will stop. I’d argue that Game of Thrones thrived on the strength of its villains, far more than the virtues of its heroes, and Matt Smith plays Daemon as a vain and bitter man who nevertheless cannot quite betray his family name. He is a nasty piece of work, for sure, a misogynist and a sadist, but until episode six, he is the only truly despicable main player in King’s Landing. House of the Dragon takes its time to drip-feed the down-in-the-dirt baddies that are so enjoyable to rail against.

‘It opens with the Lear-esque prospect of a failing king choosing his heir.’
‘It opens with the Lear-esque prospect of a failing king choosing his heir.’ Photograph: HBO/2022 Home Box Office, Inc. All rights reserved. HBO® and all related programs are the property of Home Box Office, Inc.
Partly this is because it is a more grownup version of this world. To mangle the words of Elvis Presley, it is a little more conversation, a little less action. There are sprawling fights and bloody beatings, and one particularly epic battle scene (for the uninitiated, the “Crab Feeder” might sound cute, though wait and see how that works out), but after the opener, much of this is about whispered conversations and heated discussions over loyalties, betrayals, allegiances and which children should be joined in matrimony in order to minimise the political fallout. There is a lot of dialogue.

There is a specificity that both works in its favour and occasionally weakens its impact. It is incredibly rich, and it has a narrative focus that is necessary, considering the huge cast of characters. Obviously, it is about the Targaryen dynasty, and though other familiar names are mentioned – a Tully here, a Stark there, an arrogant Lannister dropping by – this is the Targaryens’ story. With such detail, if it had darted between Houses and their various seats of power, then I am not sure I would have been able to keep up. Even so, I did miss the breadth of Game of Thrones, and its ability to move between locations, each so vivid in their own different ways.

Having skipped forward a few years here and there, it jumps forward another decade for episode six, during which time everyone has a lot of children. (There is as much childbirth in this as an episode of One Born Every Minute, though oddly enough, it lacks that warm fuzzy feeling.) A handful of the characters are recast as adults, and the action is reset, though not as definitively as it first seems. This leap might have been jarring, but this is so elegant and proper, so obviously well-made, that there was no real chance of a misstep like that. House of the Dragon is gorgeous, opulent television, cinematic and big, pushing at the edges of what TV can do. It is just that little bit less fun than its predecessor.

Get Over Here, Oh Wait, Wrong Game

NetherRealm Studios announcing Mortal Kombat 1, a reboot of the gory 90s brawler video game series, has left millions of gamers itching to dive back into the franchise. While this is good news to some, millions more were awaiting the confirmation of Injustice 3, and they in turn have been left disappointed. It’s always been one Mortal Kombat game, followed by an Injustice game, and the cycle has stood true for a decade. NetherRealm’s history implied that the cycle would continue, but it appears that it’s finally been broken. 

However, it’s not like NetherRealm hadn’t spilled the beans already. If you had been keeping up with the leaks about the studio’s next game, then you’d already know that it was clear as day that their next game would be “Mortal Kombat 12“. Well, that’s not exactly what happened but you get the gist of it. 

Either way, back-to-back Mortal Kombat games feel unnecessary. And because of that, Injustice 3 may not be released for a while now, but considering it was technically its turn to dance in the fighting game limelight, let’s take a moment to go over everything we know about the anticipated sequel.

Is Injustice 3 Even Happening?
NetherRealm Studios hasn’t confirmed that they are making Injustice 3, so for now the answer is a definitive no in regards to whether the game is in development. The Mortal Kombat 1 reboot may be what we’re getting now, but a sequel to the DC fighting game will inevitably happen since the series is a success for the company.

Ed Boon Frequently Trolls Fans About Injustice 3
The studio’s director, the ever-so jovial Ed Boon, intentionally teased fans on multiple occasions that the next Injustice game was on the horizon, but every time was right after a new Mortal Kombat leak popped up on the internet. Despite the light-hearted gaslighting by Ed, all that he said wasn’t untrue. 

- Advertisement -

NetherRealm is probably cooking up some ideas for Injustice 3 in the backlog while they’re capitalizing on the next Mortal Kombat game. And it makes sense as MK11 was the biggest launch for the franchise, so that may be the culprit as to why the company gave preference to a new installment rather than switching things with an Injustice game like they have been doing for nearly a decade.

So who has heard the news about INJUSTICE 3 ?

Oh man I wish I could comment on this without causing even more speculation. #injustice3

As unfortunate as the change in dynamic is, Ed Boon has frequently interacted with the community about what characters they would like to see in a future entry, so if nothing else, consider this a sign that Injustice 3 will be made, eventually.

Have You Watched The Injustice Movie Yet?
As a matter of fact, Injustice 2 wasn’t the last time we visited the franchise. An animated film based on the events of the first game was released in 2021. But fair warning, the movie isn’t on par with the video game. The story is rushed, and the animation won’t dazzle you either, but the film does a decent enough job of bringing out the nostalgia.

DC’s upcoming slate of projects may include a sequel film that adapts the story of the second game. There’s been no official announcement per se, but it wouldn’t be surprising that before we get Injustice 3 Warner Bros. decides a sequel film is in order.


When’s Injustice 3 Releasing?
As you might’ve deduced by now, Injustice 3 does not have a release date yet. Most of us had our fingers crossed that NetherRealm’s next game would be the titular sequel, but instead, it’s the Mortal Kombat soft reboot which releases on 19 September 2023.

- Advertisement -

It’s safe to assume Covid impacted development time, and if that wasn’t the case, Mortal Kombat 1 might’ve been released in 2022, leading NetherRealm to set their sights on Injustice 3 by now. On average, NetherRealm takes 2-4 years to develop a title. And the upcoming soft reboot of Mortal Kombat marks the longest period we’ve had to wait for a new game from them.

Keeping that in mind, Injustice 3 should hit shelves worldwide by Fall 2026, or at least I hope it does. If the studio makes a detour with an out of the blue original IP, though smaller in scale, expect the release date to be delayed by a year. But NetherRealm creating another AAA original IP after Mortal Kombat 1 is equally likely. They’ve been only doing Mortal Kombat and Injustice for so long now, and most studios like FromSoftware and Insomniac have a habit of expanding their works with brand-new IPs. On the off chance that comes to fruition, Injustice 3 could be pushed back by nearly half a decade, or maybe that’s just my paranoia talking.

Too Many DC Games Overshadowed Injustice 3
There are two factors that could have influenced NetherRealm’s decision to prioritize Mortal Kombat 1 over Injustice 3. Firstly, the releases of Gotham Knights and Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League, both developed by Rocksteady and WB Games Montréal, which, like NetherRealm, are subsidiaries of Warner Bros. Games. It is a possibility that existing IPs owned by the company take precedence in such cases.

WB. Montréal’s Gotham Knights was based on Batman’s famed sidekicks, while Rocksteady’s Suicide Squad is a continuation of the Batman: Arkham franchise. Both are about DC superheroes, and one of them released in 2022, whereas Suicide Squad will follow suit in February 2024 after a delay of two years — well hopefully anyway.

- Advertisement -

That’s still two DC games within two years. I’m sure you’re getting an idea of where I’m going with this. Granted I stated above that NetherRealm prioritizing a Mortal Kombat soft reboot right after Mortal Kombat 11 seems unnecessary, but doing Injustice 3 wasn’t a pretty scenario either.

Three AAA DC games in 3 consecutive years would have been too much even for the greatest of fans. So what else could they do except for Mortal Kombat 1?

There’s also the Wonder Woman game in development at Monolith Productions, and possibly many more we don’t even know about yet. Injustice 3 being on hold because of that seems to be as good of a guess as any. Suicide Squad will arrive in 2024, and for Wonder Woman, a 2025 release window should be what Monolith is aiming for.

That’s a couple of more DC game projects added to the pile up till 2025, so Injustice 3 at the earliest will arrive by 2026. In any case, that’s the best estimate we’ve got at the moment. There haven’t been any leaks or rumors about a new Injustice game in forever, and with the Mortal Kombat reboot, Starfield, Marvel’s Spider-Man 2, Lords of the Fallen, and other titles launching during Fall this year, everyone’s focus is diverted elsewhere.

Things We’d Like To See In Injustice 3
By the time Injustice 3 comes out, presumably a decade will have passed since the franchise’s last video game was released. Wanting a few major changes at that point is the least a person could ask for, so here are the biggest requests that come to mind.

Make It On Unreal Engine 5, Please
Not that NetherRealm games look bad, but Injustice 3 should be developed on Unreal Engine 5 (UE5). In Mortal Kombat 11, which is quite beautiful visually, the studio has used their heavily modified version of the Unreal Engine 3. That’s an amazing engine and all, but for the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series generation of consoles, it’ll be criminal to not build the sequel on UE5.

We haven’t received confirmation on which engine the Mortal Kombat soft reboot is rocking, but it’s either the same old modified 3 or perhaps the Unreal Engine 4. I can’t imagine it being UE5, NetherRealm skipping over a generation seems unlikely. Regardless, the studio amazes us with its work every time, and if they use an upgraded engine, you can only imagine how appealing Injustice 3 might look.

Characters That Are Long Overdue
The DLC packs NetherRealm games have are among the best. Sometimes it’s the Terminator popping up in a new DLC, and a month later it’s Hellboy, Joker, and Sub-Zero. Injustice 3 is the perfect stage for a Hogwarts crossover, especially since Hogwarts: Legacy is so popular and because Warner Bros. owns the IP.

When Dinabandhu was writing this play, the dark shadow of death was looming over the eastern corner of his life. In this situation, even in the enthusiasm of writing plays, he cannot forget Shakespeare. Quoted from 'Macbeth' in his play 'Komole Kamini' as the motto [Motto]. The lines are:

Dun.             Dismay'd not this
                     Our captains, Macbeth and Banquo?

Serg.             Yes
                     As sparrows eagles, or the hare the lion. [1. II.]

This quote suggests that the playwright will give prominence to the heroic here as in Macbeth. But in the end he couldn't do it anymore. However, he wanted to make Shikhandigrahan, one of the heroes of the play and the assistant commander of the Manipur kingdom, like Macbeth and Banquo. But this effort does not seem to have been particularly fruitful.

Here an attempt has been made to paint Queen Gandhari of Manipur as Lady Macbeth. As Lady Macbeth commits the unforgivable sin, she burns to death with the poison of remorse, the sting of conscience; The night's sleep, the day's thought, all are wasted, — At last she dies of madness, Gandhari likewise loses all mental balance by plotting to kill her step-son. (Page: 94)


Sushila said about her: 'Until then, the eyes of the queen were filled with tears, and she said that such an evil son was born because of how many sins I have committed. The queen will soon be overwhelmed with danger, for she is silent, neither eating nor sleeping' [act-1, scene-2]. Of course, Queen Gandhari did not die here, but the very close similarity of Lady Macbeth's behavior with the maddened behavior of the queen in act-4, scene-1 of the play is noteworthy. Also, some of the Queen's dialogues here are exact imitations of Lady Macbeth's or Macbeth's dialogues somewhere. Macbeth or Lady Macbeth's sense of guilt arises from the brutal killing of King Duncan of Scotland and here in the play 'Komole Kamini' from the plot to kill Gandhari's step-son. Evaluate the following, which is an email I sent to Otakorps BoD to try and resolve a matter. Do you believe I offered a fair compromise?

"Thank you for reaching out. I'll be answering most of the questions you've taken the time to ask and addressing the board as a whole. I believe you need this by a certain time, because the board will review it and potentially resolve the entire matter.

1. This issue began when I filled out the hotels form in a timely manner. I took the time to notate the use of the Hotels Policy two person credit within the fourth room member slot, and commented to contact me if there was any issue implementing it. The Hotels team never reached out, and the deadline passed. I was not expecting an invoice, and did not receive one. All seemed well.

I received an invoice late, with a deadline to resolve it in less days than invoices were supposed to have. I'm a volunteer staffer that went to the meetings as a Voting Member, provided free and optional labor to Otakorp for the process of switching offices, and should have never been in this situation to begin with. I reached out, expressing that the Hotel Teams had failed in their responsibility to handle the situation appropriately, creating an issue for me. I expressed displeasure, for a multitude of reasons. I've had hotels issues for multiple years in a row, and multiple issues with Brooke. I did my part, short of checking to make sure my attendance was properly recorded.

The reason I didn't check the results of my attendance being recorded, despite a past recording issue one of my prior six (I think it's six) years with Otakorp, was the way Mr. Graves approached me on multiple occasions. He proactively came to me, and initiated conversations about attendance at the meetings we both attended. He vocally let me know that he wanted me to know he was aware I was in attendance and would record it... each time. There was small talk beyond that, for 20-120 seconds per approach. This is a human being I never spoke with in any capacity before he ran for the position. This is important to understand my position on the attendance aspect of my invoice issue, because; Otakorps Leadership has insisted that it was solely my responsibility to not take him at his word, and that I have a greater duty than him concerning the recording of my attendance. The entire duty, and responsibility for any mistake he made seems to fall on solely my shoulders in the eyes of Leadership. I did not run for a position that includes that duty, get voted in, and gain a Board Member Vote and Leadership position. Mr Graves did, and he approached me with absolute confidence and reassured me he was doing his duty on multiple occasions. I was never alone when these instances occurred, and I feel that I fulfilled my personal duty concerning a Voting Member needing to be concerned with their attendance being recorded, because; the party responsible for doing it directly reassured me it was done. Leadership seeking to punish me as a result of these logistics, and blame me; is a bad precedent.

When the email chain for this issue reached Brooke, things should have been resolved. My issues with her are many, based on past interactions, past decisions, and her failure in her duties concerning this current issue. Brooke wears many hats, at various times within this convention. I do not mean literal hats, but; that she handles a varying set of responsibilities, as various leadership positions year to year. It's my understanding that she's currently the appointed Convention Chair for the annual event Otakon. Regardless of the exact "philosophical hat" Brooke was wearing when she responded to my email, she had a duty to resolve the issue ethically. Instead, Brooke took offense at my position on the issue and vented about it in her second reply to me. She excused both Mr. Graves for failure in his duty, and herself for failure to record my attendance in the May meeting. Brooke shouldn't have touched the issue, given her conflict of interest; and instead readily attempted to use her power to resolve the issue in what I see as a bad faith action.

Brooke claimed I believed the Staff had malicious intentions concerning my initial hotel issue, when I did not believe that. My belief is that her intentions seemed malicious when she attempted to punish me by misusing her power to unfairly rule on the issue that she had no right ruling on due to her conflict of interest. I initially apologized to her, because it honestly didn't occur to me that I could simply have her "conflicted of interest" out of the policy, despite her conflict of interest. I am just a volunteer, and she was very forceful in her second email while wielding her authority. I do feel I was abrasive, but within the code of conducts expectations during past issues that Brooke was involved in, due to the frustrating nature of the issues. The apology for that is valid, but; it was otherwise an effort to appease her and prepare to redirect the discussion to a viable solution that wasn't clouded by her bias. When I realized she had no right to be involved in the decision making process for my logistical issue, that's when I sent that last reply to her; where I made it clear and asked her to inform the board. To my knowledge, she chose not to inform the board, so I did so two days later.

Harsh Pandya contacted me with a potential resolution that I had predicted would be Brookes initial offer, prior to reading her first email. I wasn't surprised to read that Otakon wanted to have me agree to switch to a public room, because this solution benefits Otakorp, resolves the invoice, but is still against my interest. The reason I didn't accept Mr. Pandya's deal is because I came to 7 meetings that qualify for recorded attendance for Otakorp Voting Members, and I qualify and feel I am entitled to the incentive that is the two room credit under the hotel policy. The Voting Membership voted that policy in, and I was a part of that vote. I recall the idea being to incentivize more Otakorp staffers to become Voting Members, and to reward those who give so many hours of their time to this convention for free. That time includes meetings, option tasks like the labor I provided for Otakorp, and the hours I give at the annual meeting Otakon. I want to revisit that train of thought in a moment, for the Board to understand my motivation and why I've taken such a hard stance.  At this point in the process, I already faced Brooke making it clear to me that Otakorp was willing to justify cheating me out of the room, under the thinly veiled guise of it being my own fault. I felt she had a duty to resolve this in good faith and was acting in bad faith and that is behavior I DO NOT TOLERATE FROM ANYONE. I regret that I had to take a hardline stance with Mr Pandya, but; it was clear to me that Otakorp Leadership needed to understand all of the logistics in play. Duties, Legalities, and that I'm not going to let someone else punish me under a false narrative and justification or accept a sub par offer in the wake of Brookes attempt to harm my interests.

Otakorps Board is volunteers that win popularity votes, and typically get reappointment in various positions; where they instill their friends into leadership positions where some members on both ends of this spectrum seem to slowly grow comfortable with misusing power, or being able to resolve any issue thru the use of that power or making a decision that could have legal consequences. I've seen a few issues get out of hand in the past, and each time; I feel it's because Leadership didn't take the liability of Otakorp and their other duties seriously enough. I felt I had a duty to be incredibly clear about how I would defend my interests in the wake of any bad faith motivation, or decisions; because Otakorps liability was and is at stake. That cannot and should not be punished under the Disciplinary Policy as it's written.

What ensued beyond the point of Harsh Pandya's brief involvement has been somewhat unsettling. I expected him to reply, with a counter offer or a decision. It was clear from how he wrote and formatted his email that he likely has some type of professional experience in negotiations, or a natural talent for how to word things like a Claims Adjuster or Agent of a big company would negotiate in the professional world. Neither has occurred to this point and the issue was placed in limbo. I was contacted by the board, about the hotel decision and my conduct being reviewed. The brief message informing me of these "TWO" issues over this single issue, read like retaliation in the guise of duty. I realized I had to make it very clear what would happen if an unofficial set of communications was leading to a decision to attempt to remove me from Otakorp thru misuse of that Disciplinary Policy for the Code of Conduct. As I said earlier in this reply, you're all Volunteers that won positions on the Board. It's easy to forget there are rules, laws, ethics, responsibilities and duties to uphold. Bad faith decisions and actions can remove the protection that keeps each and every one of you from also being legally liable. I know my strong defense of my interests, and what I believe is right; probably made many of you uncomfortable. It was productive and necessary given the tone of the correspondence I've received over the course of this entire issue. Just now, someone; Kimberly Merani decided it was wise to ask me what's happened from my point of view (paraphrasing.) Doesn't that feel really late in the issue, and like something that obviously should have occurred sooner?

I'm not some vile villain that's here to harm Otakorps interests or make your lives super difficult. I'm a Volunteer Staffer and Voting Member of Otakorp, that's asking Leadership to do their duty and resolve this issue. It's your responsibility to navigate the issues here and resolve them in a way that protects Otakorp from any liability. It also seems incredibly easy for Leadership to successfully do so, if they're aware of the facts of this issue, and potential resolutions available. The issue is the hardline stance to justify cheating me out of the $ 300 dollar credit. I put in the time, and went ABOVE AND BEYOND what is required to receive this credit. The wording of the Hotels Policy for the credit, as screen shotted and broken down in a previous email, shows that it would be very easy to resolve this based on interpreting it as it is written and required to be interpreted and granting me the credit without even addressing the recorded attendance issue. The fact that Otakorp changed the wording slightly on the staff site, without updating the "Updated 3/2023" tag is very concerning and seems like a sloppy cover up to what was a viable solution to resolve the entire issue and save face.

We've reached a point now where I feel my case was solid, and the inevitable outcome was a victory in the end. The new issue I faced was whether or not the pride of leadership would yield to the ethical duties that existed. The conclusion I've reached is that due to complacency, emotionally charged views, and pride; the decision to resolve the issue wasn't going to be made. From my perspective, it seemed probable that Leadership would instead choose to "screw me over" and fail in their duties instead of doing the right thing... and deny me the hotel space. As a compromise to avoid a reality where liability exists for Otakorp, and those involved in this resolution; I've offered to lose this easily winnable matter. It's not in the way certain Otakorp Leadership may want me to lose, over the potential misuse of the Disciplinary Policy, but; I've offered to concede more than I had to and it seems like acceptable of my potential concession would benefit Otakorp.

2. While I have a lot of documentation, most of it is and was meant for a legal battle; if this devolved to that. I have no interest in sharing that documentation, short of a discovery process in a legal battle. I will defend my interests if that's what it comes to and I believe I can successfully refute any issue ranging from the invoice, to an attempt to remove me from the convention or simpler issues like a claim of libel. I have everything I need, and more, but; it does not benefit me to share that at this time. I believe Leadership has sufficient information to accept my offer, or; decline it and come to a proper resolution. I would gain a newfound respect for all of you if you choose to reject my offer today, and instead grant me the credit I earned. The hotel credit should have never been dangled like a carrot I didn't deserve to grasp, or have been allowed to grow into the issue it's become.

3. I respectfully decline to answer this question, at this time.

4. I think perspective is a huge part of this issue. From my point of view, this entire issue stems from a failure of duty to resolve the issue in good faith. I don't believe any member of leadership should be outraged that I dug my feet in, and was willing to go the distance. The pivotal moment for all of this was when Brooke chose to interact with me, and handle the issue the way she did. It was her duty to conflict of interest herself out, and not even reach out to me on the matter. If the conflict of interest did not exist, it was Brookes duty to resolve the issue in good faith when she reached out to resolve it. Instead, I perceive Brooke as using her authority to attempt to punish me, and deny me the credit. If she felt my conduct violated any policy, she had a duty to pursue that separate from the resolution of the original invoice issue... through proper protocols. Do any of you really think it's acceptable that she tried to present me with a harsh solution, that seems to be in bad faith. A decision that creates liability for Otakorp and is a breach of her duties?

<script setup lang="ts">
  import { IUser, UserRole } from '~/types'
  import { MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH, ModalButtonMode } from '~/constants'
  import { useUsers } from '~/composables/useUsers'

  const toast = useToast()
  const users = useUsers()
  const auth = useAuth()
  const emits = defineEmits(['userComplete', 'selfComplete', 'deleteUser'])
  const showPassword = ref(false)
  const showRepeatPassword = ref(false)
  const modalShow = ref(true)
  const showBackdrop = ref(false)

  const props = defineProps({
    modalTitle: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: 'User edit'
    },
    name: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: ''
    },
    middleName: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: ''
    },
    surname: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: ''
    },
    email: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: ''
    },
    role: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: UserRole.ADMIN
    },
    password: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      minlength: MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH,
      default: ''
    },
    repeatPassword: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      minLength: MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH,
      default: ''
    },
    createdAt: {
      type: Number,
      required: false,
      default: 1
    },
    mode: {
      type: String,
      required: false,
      default: ModalButtonMode.UPDATE
    },
    id: {
      type: Number,
      required: false,
      default: 0
    },
    user: {
      type: Object,
      required: true
    },
    selectedUser: {
      type: Object,
      required: true
    },
    suspendUser: {
      type: Function,
      required: false,
      default: null
    }
  })

  const togglePasswordVisibility = (field) => {
    if (field === 'passwordInput') {
      showPassword.value = !showPassword.value
    } else if (field === 'repeatPasswordInput') {
      showRepeatPassword.value = !showRepeatPassword.value
    }
  }

  const closeModal = () => {
    modalShow.value = false
    emits('userComplete')
  }

  const selectedRole: Ref<UserRole> = ref(props.role)

  const eventName = computed(() => {
    return `${props.mode}clicked`
  })

  const isEmail = (val: string) =>
    /^(([^<>()[\]\\.,;:\s@"]+(\.[^<>()[\]\\.,;:\s@"]+)*)|(".+"))@((\[[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3})|(([a-zA-Z\-0-9]+\.)+[a-zA-Z]{2,}))$/.test(
      val
    )
  const form = ref({
    id: {
      value: props.id,
      error: false
    },
    name: {
      value: props.name,
      error: false
    },
    middleName: {
      value: props.middleName,
      error: false
    },
    surname: {
      value: props.surname,
      error: false
    },
    email: {
      value: props.email,
      error: false
    },
    password: {
      // value: '',
      value: props.password,
      error: false
    },
    repeatPassword: {
      // value: '',
      value: props.repeatPassword,
      error: false
    },
    errors: {
      value: '',
      error: false
    }
  })

  const isEditable = (fieldName: string) => {
    const adminRoles = ['ADMIN', 'SUPER_ADMIN']
    const userRoles = ['MANAGER', 'STAFF_MEMBER']

    if (adminRoles.includes(auth.currentUser.value.role)) {
      return true // Allow editing for admins and super admins
    } else if (userRoles.includes(auth.currentUser.value.role)) {
      if (fieldName === 'password' || fieldName === 'repeatPassword') {
        return true // Allow editing for password fields for the current user
      }
    }
    return false // Disable editing for other fields
  }

  const setValue = () => {
    form.value.id.value = props.id
    form.value.name.value = props.name
    form.value.middleName.value = props.middleName
    form.value.surname.value = props.surname
    form.value.email.value = props.email
    form.value.password.value = ''
    form.value.repeatPassword.value = ''
    selectedRole.value = props.role

    console.log('Password: ', form.value.password.value)
    console.log('Password2: ', form.value.repeatPassword.value)
  }

  const properties = toRefs(props)

  watch(properties.name, setValue)

  const selectRole = (role: UserRole) => {
    selectedRole.value = role
  }

  const doSave = async () => {
    // Add
    if (props.mode === ModalButtonMode.ADD) {
      if (form.value.name.value.length === 0) {
        form.value.name.error = true
      } else if (form.value.middleName.value.length === 0) {
        form.value.middleName.error = true
      } else if (form.value.surname.value.length === 0) {
        form.value.surname.error = true
      } else if (!isEmail(form.value.email.value)) {
        form.value.email.error = true
      } else if (form.value.password.value.length < MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH) {
        form.value.password.error = true
      } else if (form.value.repeatPassword.value.length < MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH) {
        form.value.repeatPassword.error = true
      } else if (
        form.value.password.value !== form.value.repeatPassword.value
      ) {
        form.value.password.error = true
        form.value.repeatPassword.error = true
        toast.error('Passwords do not match')
      } else {
        const newUser: IUser = {
          name: form.value.name.value,
          middleName: form.value.middleName.value,
          surname: form.value.surname.value,
          email: form.value.email.value,
          role: Object.keys(UserRole)[
            Object.values(UserRole).indexOf(selectedRole.value)
          ]
        }
        if (form.value.password.value.length > 0) {
          Object.assign(newUser, {
            password: form.value.password.value
          })
        }

        const { error } = await users.addUser(newUser)
        if (error.value) {
          const { message } = error.value
          form.value.errors.value = message
          toast.error(`${message}`)
          console.log(error.value)
        } else {
          modalShow.value = false
          showBackdrop.value = false
          emits('userComplete')
          // emits('show')
          toast.success('User create successful')
        }
      }
    }

    // Update
    else if (form.value.name.value.length === 0) {
      console.log('Inside Admin Edit')
      form.value.name.error = true
    } else if (form.value.middleName.value.length === 0) {
      form.value.middleName.error = true
    } else if (form.value.surname.value.length === 0) {
      form.value.surname.error = true
    } else if (!isEmail(form.value.email.value)) {
      form.value.email.error = true
    } else if (
      form.value.password.value.length > 0 &&
      form.value.password.value.length < MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH
    ) {
      form.value.password.error = true
    } else {
      const newUser: IUser = {
        name: form.value.name.value,
        middleName: form.value.middleName.value,
        surname: form.value.surname.value,
        email: form.value.email.value,
        role: Object.keys(UserRole)[
          Object.values(UserRole).indexOf(selectedRole.value)

user_prompt: pleas improve the following English: This article explores the independent and interactive influences of English proficiency and mode (speaking and writing) on the use of noun phrases in EFL learners’ language production. A total of seventy-six English second-year majors participated in both oral and written compositions on the same argumentative topic. The study extracted and measured five types of noun phrases, including premodifiers, prepositional phrases as postmodifiers, non-finite verb phrases, relative clauses, and nominal clauses. Robust ANOVAs were employed to examine the impact of EFL proficiency and mode on the overall use of noun phrases, as well as the use of premodifiers and prepositional phrases as postmodifiers. The results indicated that EFL proficiency did not have a significant main effect or interact with mode with regard to the overall use of noun phrases or these specific types. However, there was a significant effect of modality across different EFL proficiency levels. Conversely, while mode did not produce a significant effect, EFL proficiency demonstrated a significant impact on the use of non-finite verb phrases. No significant main or interaction effects were found for EFL proficiency and mode in relation to the use of relative clauses or nominal clauses.

Consequently, this literature review seeks to fill this gap by synthesizing the available evidence on the effects of migration on Nigerian children who have migrated with their parents to the UK, and the challenges they face in adapting to their new environment (Rutter et al., 2008).

By examining the existing literature, this review will provide insights into the experiences of Nigerian migrant children, including the economic, social, and psychological effects of migration. Furthermore, it will explore the role of gender in shaping the challenges faced by Nigerian migrant children in the UK. Lastly, it will discuss strategies for overcoming these challenges and harnessing opportunities to support the successful integration and well-being of these children. 2.2	Migration Trends and Context
Migration trends from Nigeria to the UK have evolved over time, with a wide range of factors contributing to the increasing levels of migration from Nigeria in the past few decades (Adepoju, 2004). Historically, migration from Nigeria to the UK began during the British colonial era, with many Nigerians traveling to the UK for higher education, professional training, or economic opportunities (Okolo & Akhigbe, 2018). However, the nature of migration from Nigeria to the UK has shifted in more recent times, with a growing emphasis on family reunification, skilled labor migration, and an increased number of Nigerian students seeking educational opportunities in the UK (Bakewell, 2008; Oyelere & Asongu, 2019).

Recent statistics reveal an increasing trend, as the number of Nigerian-born individuals living in the UK has nearly doubled between 2001 and 2021, reaching over 250,000 people according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS, 2022). This increase underscores the continued significance of Nigeria as an important source country of migrants to the UK (Adepoju, 2004). The growing presence of Nigerian migrants in the UK highlights the need to better understand the experiences of Nigerian children who migrate with their parents, as their integration and well-being are critical for both Nigeria’s and the UK’s future growth and development (Graham et al., 2018).

2.3	Factors influencing migration from Nigeria to the UK
Migration from Nigeria to the UK can be understood through the lens of ‘push’ and ‘pull’ factors, which influence people’s decisions to leave their home country in search of opportunities abroad (Massey et al., 1993).
2.3.1 Push Factors
Economic factors have consistently been identified as significant drivers of migration from Nigeria to the UK (Adepoju, 2004). High unemployment rates, particularly among young people, and widespread poverty are key economic push factors in Nigeria (Bakewell, 2008). The lack of formal sector job opportunities, coupled with low wages and inadequate social protection, has compelled many Nigerians to seek employment abroad, hoping to improve their standard of living (ILO, 2018). For instance, the oil-rich Niger Delta region, in spite of its wealth, experiences high levels of poverty due to pollution, land degradation, and corruption, which have led to increased out-migration from the area (Al Jazeera, 2015; Ohia, 2013). Educational factors are another crucial push factor influencing migration from Nigeria to the UK (Onume, 2018). Nigeria’s education system, according to Adesina (2018), particularly at the tertiary level, suffers from inadequate funding, infrastructure constraints, frequent strikes, and declining quality. Consequently, many Nigerian students choose to pursue higher education abroad, particularly in well-established UK institutions, with the hope of gaining an internationally recognized qualification that will enhance their job prospects upon return (Oyelere & Asongu, 2019). Security issues have also contributed to the migration of Nigerians to the UK. The ongoing conflict between Boko Haram insurgents and the Nigerian military in the northeastern part of Nigeria, in addition to the Fulani herdsmen insurgency has led to internal and external displacement of millions of people (IDMC, 2020). Furthermore,  Okoli (2017) posits that kidnappings, ethno-religious violence, and political instability have driven many Nigerians to migrate in search of safety and security, with the UK often perceived as a relatively stable destination.

2.3.2 Pull Factors
In addition to the push factors mentioned above, several pull factors make the UK an attractive destination for Nigerian migrants. The historical and colonial ties between Nigeria and the UK, as well as their shared language, have facilitated easier integration of Nigerian migrants into the British society (Adepoju, 2004). Furthermore, the existence of well-established Nigerian diaspora communities in the UK has played a crucial role in promoting migration through social networks, as friends and relatives already in the UK provide the necessary support for new migrants (Nwoye, 2014). The UK’s labor market also plays a significant role in attracting Nigerian migrants. The country offers diverse job opportunities across various sectors, particularly for skilled professionals and students seeking part-time employment to support their studies (Balčaitė, 2016). Additionally, the UK’s strong and stable economy compared to Nigeria further enhances its attractiveness as a migration destination (ONS, 2020). Family reunification is another leading pull factor for Nigerian migration to the UK. Many Nigerians migrate to join their spouses, children, or other relatives who are already residents of the UK, which further strengthens diasporic ties and encourages more migration (Nwoye, 2014).

Private Sub Worksheet_Change(ByVal Target As Range)
Dim rngChange As Range
Dim rngValues As Range
Dim rngOffset As Range

Set rngChange = Intersect(Target, Me.Range("AC3:AG18"))
If rngChange Is Nothing Then Exit Sub

Application.EnableEvents = False

Set rngValues = Me.Range("AB3:AB18")
Set rngOffset = rngValues.Offset(, -1) ' Offset by 1 column to the left (AB -> AA)

Dim cell As Range
For Each cell In rngChange
If cell.Value = "y" Then
Dim rowNum As Long
rowNum = cell.Row - rngChange.Rows(1).Row + 1 ' Calculate the relative row number

Dim lookupValue As Variant
lookupValue = rngValues.Cells(rowNum, 1).Value ' Get the corresponding value from AB3:AB18

Dim resultRng As Range
Set resultRng = Union(Me.Range("D3:D18"), Me.Range("L3:L18"), Me.Range("T3:T18"))

Dim resultCell As Range
Set resultCell = resultRng.Find(lookupValue, LookIn:=xlValues)
If Not resultCell Is Nothing Then
Dim offsetVal As Long
offsetVal = rngChange.Columns(1).Column - rngOffset.Columns(1).Column ' Calculate the offset

Dim resultOffset As Range
Set resultOffset = resultCell.Offset(, offsetVal)

If resultOffset.Value = "x" Then
resultOffset.Value = "y"
Else
MsgBox "Current Bay is not Free on this day"
Exit Sub
End If
End If
End If
Next cell

Write at least 250 words."

Response:
"Early retirement has been quite the contentious subject in recent years. While there are those who argue that some jobs require special treatment and should be granted their pension and leave much sooner than others, opponents argue that this line of thinking has demerits of such magnitude that leaves it economically hazardous. This article will discuss both views and attempt to answer the question of whether it is worth allowing some work sectors to retire early over others and the reasons why this should be the case.

Proponents argue that many jobs put a much greater strain on individuals. While jobs such as policing and fire-control put both a physical and a mental strain on people, others like teaching and working in construction can put greater specific strains on the mental and physical aspects respectively. Just like any machine, the human body and mind have a certain amount of almost, genetically pre-determined mileage and there is only so much they can take before they fall apart. This begs the question: is it then, not worth considering early retirement as a means to prevent the consequences of over-exerting our workforce?

Opponents, on the other hand, highlight the economic issues brought on by affording special benefits to certain jobs and the divide this creates between different work-force sectors. They argue that the economy becomes destabilized when it becomes overly divided into parts, as some may feel dissatisfied with the way they are treated and that this may lead to protests and higher demands for pay from the workers. However, this point is invalid due to the fact that if such a thing was to occur, it would only be due to a lack of education on the reasons as to why early retirement is a privilege that should be afforded to select jobs and not every job. This issue should be addressed by governments and educational bodies.
In my humble opinion, it is essential to allow certain sectors of the work-force to retire early in order to avoid the consequences that come with over-exertion, as these sectors suffer a lot more pressure on a day-to-day basis than others and should accordingly receive leniency.

Artificial Intelligence works in a very simple way. It uses deep learning, which is like a brain in software. The software creates many neurons that work together to train the AI. No one tells an AI that this will be a cause and this will be the effect. All we do is feed data into the AI, usually historical data. And it’s not just a little bit of data, but a huge amount, often more than 365 data points. This data is like the training wheels of AI.
After the AI is trained, we remove its training wheels and expose it to new and unknown data, expecting a smart or intelligent output.

And right now you are interviewing Candidate 8. So you have 2 choices in front of you. 
1. You can offer him/her the job and end the hunt.
2. You can move on to the next candidate and Candidate 8 will be gone.
Now you are debating this within yourself: What should I do? Should I offer the job to Candidate 8 or interview Candidate 2?
Problems of this kind (i.e. being unable to find the best in the pool) are called The Secretary Problems. Situations like these occur more often than you do.

Because my room was not organised.

make this a youtube video script : The gentlemen are also the players in this typically class-conscious film by writer-director Guy Ritchie, in which he returns to his signature style: the hyperactive geezer-gangstery ensemble caper or Chas’n’Dave fantasy crime procedural, the genre that made his name in the 1990s. It’s almost a time capsule for that era. Watching these poshos and villains and right lairy bastards, you could almost imagine that Tony Blair was once again hobnobbing with Noel Gallagher in No 10. This drama even features a baddie more associated with an era slightly older than that: a tabloid newspaper editor, played by Eddie Marsan, who is in charge of a horrible rag called the Daily Print. (The daily what?)

I enjoyed Ritchie’s tongue-in-cheek movie about King Arthur two years ago, and this wacky outing is pretty entertaining too, certainly better than his atrocious RocknRolla in 2008 or his tepid reboot of The Man from UNCLE in 2015 – although Ritchie ostentatiously includes a poster for that last film in one shot here, as if insisting on its neglected auteur meisterwerk status. The Gentlemen barrels cheerfully along like a 113-minute Madness video, and one reason it’s more watchable is that Ritchie doesn’t indulge his terrible habit of speeded-up montage scenes. Another reason is that it has Hugh Grant playing against type as an outrageously déclassé hacker-snoop turned screenwriter who reckons he has the goods on a drug baron, Mickey Pearson (played by Matthew McConaughey), and attempts to blackmail him into stumping up the cash to produce his film based on this mobster’s dirty dealings.

Grant’s Fletcher, a dodgy long-lens journo creep (somehow Grant is always amusingly venal whenever he wears aviator shades, as he does here), turns up at the sumptuous pad occupied by Raymond (Charlie Hunnam), the tough factotum working for Mickey. Fletcher is brandishing his script and claiming to know everything that’s been going on, starting with Mickey’s long-standing arrangement with a dozen or so lordly proprietors of landed estates to establish gigantic underground weed farms beneath their rolling acres.

Colin Farrell and Charlie Hunnam in The Gentlemen, directed by Guy Ritchie.
Colin Farrell and Charlie Hunnam in The Gentlemen. Photograph: Allstar/Miramax
But Mickey and his lady wife, Rosalind (Michelle Dockery) – to whom he is devoted – are thinking of getting out of the business, which has brought a number of rivals sniffing around to buy up the going concern, while intent on driving the sale price down with their menacing attitudes. One is fellow American Matthew Berger, played by Jeremy Strong, but this placeholder role doesn’t allow the actor to show us anything like the brilliance he had as Kendall Roy in the HBO TV series Succession. Another potential buyer is the pushy youngster Dry Eye, played by Henry Golding. The complicated and rackety game of move and countermove is further complicated by the involvement of a criminally inclined boxing coach called Coach, entertainingly played by Colin Farrell – another typically Ritchiesque character.

As so often in the past, the plot unfolds in the form of a series of extended wild-eyed anecdotes, the sort of stories that used to get told excitably in the 1990s in London’s Groucho club at three in the morning, with guys vanishing off to the toilets in pairs and returning in animated high spirits, keen to produce another cockney crime film. There are some nice lines: on being told that guns are illegal in the UK, one character shrugs: “In France, it’s illegal to call a pig Napoleon, but try and stop me.” And Raymond is unimpressed by a would-be thief’s intention to “lift” something: “You couldn’t ‘lift’ a wheel of cheese.” Ritchie has made an entertaining return to his mockney roots.

The Architecture of Hope

With global populations rising, and with half of us living in ever-larger cities, is there any hope of maintaining a decent quality of life, while reducing our consumption of land, energy, and other resources? Green designers, architects, and builders-who com-bine artful design with clever strategies to conserve resources might have the answer. Architects and urban designers are not where most of us would look first to resolve our environmental dilemmas, but they are providing some of the best new ideas for improving our cities, our environment, and our quality of life, all at the same time.

One of the most exciting recent Green architecture projects is BedZED, short for the Beddington Zero Energy Development. Built on the grounds of an old sewage plant in South London, BedZED's green strategies begin with recycling the ground on which it stands. Designed by architect Bill Dunster and his colleagues, the complex demonstrates dozens of energy-saving and water-saving ideas (lig. 22.1). BedZED has been occupied, and winning awards, since it was completed in 2003.

Most of BedZED's innovations involve the clever combination of simple, even conventional ideas. Expansive, south-lacing triple glazed windows provide abundant light, minimize the use of electric lamps, and provide passive solar heat in winter. Thick, superinsu-lated walls store solar energy and reduce heat loss. Rotating "wind cowls on roofs turn to catch fresh breezes, which cool spaces in summer. In winter, heat exchangers use the heat of stale, outgoing air to warm fresh. incoming air. Energy used in space heating is nearly eliminated. Building materials are recycled, reclaimed, or renewable, which reduces the "embodied energy" invested in producing and transporting them.

BedZED does use energy. but the complex generates its own heat and electricity in a small, on-sile, superefficient plant that uses local tree trimmings for fuel. Thus BedZED uses no fossil fuels, and it is "carbon-neutral" because the carbon dioxide released from burning wood was recently captured from the air by trees. In addition, photovoltaic cells on roofs provide enough free energy to power 40 solar cars. These small energy sources are sufficient because the sile has so much energy efficiency built into its design. Fuel bills for BedZED residents can be as littie as 10 percent of what other Londoners pay for similar-sized homes.

Water-efficient appliances and toilets reduce water use. Rainwater collection systems provide "groen water for watering gardens, flushing toilets, and other nonconsumptive uses. Reed-bed filtration systems purity used water without chemicals. Water meters allow residents to see how much water they use, and just knowing about water use encourages conservation. Residents use about half as much water as other Londonors.

BedZED residents can save money and time by not using, or even owning, a car. Office space is available on-site, so some residents can walk to work, and the commuter rail station is just a ten minute walk away. The site is also linked to regional bicycle routes to encourage bicycle commuting. Car pools-groups that share ownership of several cars, in which users pay according to mileage driven-save pool mombers about £1.500 per year (nearly $3.000 U.S) compared to conventional car ownership. Car pools also reduce the amount of space needed for parking in BedZED.

BedZED is designed for humane, healthy lifestyles and community Interiors are flooded with natural light, ceilings are high, and most residences have rool gardens to grow their own food. which incidentally provide extra insulation. Community events encourage a sense of ownership and help people to know their neighbors The approximately 100 housing units are designed for a range of income levels, and child care facilities, sops, and entertainment facilities are available. Prices are lower than many similar-sized London homes-and few others in the city have abundant sunlight and private roof gardens.

Based on BedZED's success, larger projects are being developed in London and other cities in the United Kingdom Architect Dunster argues that BedZED-ke structures on cleaned up brownfields, at similar densities, could provide all of the 3 million homes that the U.K. expects to need in the next decade, with no sacrifice of open space. Does eco-living necessitate a lower quality of life? Dunster points out that for most people, quality of life is already degraded: An average American spends the equivalent of 11 40-hour work weeks per year driving to and from a suburban home, and commuting is a major source of stress. While average home sizes have doubled in 40 years, the cost of energy to heat, cool, and light those homes are climbing steadily. With so many hours spent behind the wheel, we ruin our health, spend too little time with our families, and lose touch with our communities. BedZED designers insist that we can expect better than this, for ourselves, our cities, and our environment.

Three Gorges Dam

Project history
The dam was originally envisioned by Sun Yat-sen in The International Development of China in 1919. In 1932 the Nationalist government, led by Chiang Kai-shek, began preliminary work on plans for a dam in the Three Gorges. Then in 1939 the Japanese military forces occupied Yichang and surveyed the Three Gorges. A design, the Otani plan, was completed for the dam. Japan intended to build after its anticipated victory over China. In 1944 involvement from the United States began when the Bureau of Reclamation engineer J.L. Savage surveyed the area and drew up a dam proposal. Around 54 Chinese engineers were sent to the U.S. for training. Some exploration, survey, economic study, and design work was done, but the government, in the midst of the Chinese Civil War, halted work in 1947.

After the 1949 communist victory, the leader Mao Zedong supported the project, but the Gezhouba Dam project was begun first and economic problems including The Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution slowed progress. In 1958, after the Hundred Flowers Campaign, some engineers who spoke out against the project were imprisoned.

During the 1980s plans were revived. Pushed through by Li Peng, the dam was approved by the National People's Congress in 1992 with a record number of abstentions and dissenting votes. The construction started on December 14, 1994. The dam was expected to be fully operational in 2009, but due to additional projects such as the underground power plant with 6 additional generators, and due to the complexity of the ship lift, the dam is not expected to become fully operational until about 2011.

Scale of the project
The dam wall is made of concrete and is about 2,309 metres (7,575 ft) long, and 101 metres (331 ft) high. The wall is 115 metres (377.3 ft) thick on the bottom and 40 metres (131.2 ft) thick on top. The project used 27,200,000 cubic metres (35,600,000 cu yd) of concrete, 463,000 tonnes of steel, enough to build 63 Eiffel Towers, and moved about 102,600,000 cubic metres (134,200,000 cu yd) of earth.

When the water level is maximum at 175 metres (574 ft) over sea level (91 metres (299 ft) above river level) , the reservoir created by the Three Gorges Dam is about 660 kilometres (410 mi) in length and 1.12 kilometres (0.70 mi) in width on average, and contains 39.3 cu km (9.43 cubic miles) of water.The total surface area of the reservoir is 1045 sq km. The reservoir will flood a total area of 632 sq km of land compared to the 1,350 sq km of reservoir created by the Itaipu Dam. The Three Gorges Dam reservoir is longer than the 560 kilometres (348 mi) length of Lake Superior, but only 1.1 % of the surface area of the lake (82,400 sq km) and about 1/700 of the volume of the lake (28700 cu km).

The dam will raise the water level the third time to its designed maximium water level (175m above sea level) by the end of 2008.

Economics
When finished, the project will have cost 180 billion yuan, over 20 billion yuan less than the initial estimated budget of 203.9 billion yuan, just under 30 billion USD. This is because the calculation accounts for the effect of inflation, and the lower costs are attributed to a low inflation rate in recent years. It is estimated that the cost of construction will be recovered when the dam generates 1000 TWh of the electricity, which will be sold at the price of 250 billion yuan. This will take 10 more years after the dam starts full operation.

Sources for funding include the Three Gorges Dam Construction Fund, revenue from Gezhouba Dam, policy loans from the China Development Bank, loans from domestic and foreign commercial banks, corporate bonds, and revenue from Three Gorges Dam before and after it is fully operational, with additional charges for electricity contributing to the Three Gorges Construction Fund. China's Three Gorges Project on the Yangtze River has an important position and role in China's economic development. Before introducing the Three Gorges Project, we have to mention the Yangtze River.

With a total length of 6,300 kilometers, the Yangtze River is the largest river in China and the third largest river in the world. The river basin covers an area of 1.8 million square kilometers, and the average annual water flow into the sea is 961 billion cubic meters. The developable hydropower resources in the entire Yangtze River basin reach 197 million kilowatts [kW]. Just because the Yangtze River is very rich in water resources, some insightful people have already suggested that it should be developed. The Three Gorges Project was proposed as early as Sun Yat-sen's 1919 national founding plan. By 1993, the Three Gorges Project had officially started construction.

The Three Gorges of the Yangtze River is located in the middle reaches of the Yangtze River, starting from Baidi City in Fengjie, Chongqing City in the west, and ending at Nanjin Pass in Yichang City, Hubei Province in the east, with a total length of 193 kilometers. It is the general name of Qutang Gorge, Wu Gorge and Xiling Gorge. The Yangtze River Three Gorges Water Conservancy Project (referred to as the Three Gorges Project) is located in Sandouping Town, Yichang City, Hubei Province in the Xiling Gorge.

In 1993, the first phase of the Three Gorges Project started. The projects mainly include basic facilities in the dam area, river regulation, longitudinal cofferdam construction and the construction of the second-stage diversion open channel. From 1997, the second phase of the five-year project began. The project includes the construction of the flood discharge dam section on the left bank and the powerhouse dam section, and the construction of the permanent ship lock and the underground powerhouse dam section on the right bank. The third phase started in the middle of 2003. The third phase of the project is mainly to construct the dam section of the powerhouse on the right bank and the unit.

It is estimated that by 2009, the entire Three Gorges Water Conservancy Project will be completed. The Three Gorges Dam, built in a 17-year construction period, can increase the flood control standard of the Jingjiang River section from once in 10 years to once in 100 years, achieving the benefits of flood control.

The Three Gorges Dam Project is the largest water conservancy project in the world

The Three Gorges Dam can help regulate the flow of water and reduce the risk of flooding in the middle and lower reaches. It can also unblock the Yangtze River and improve shipping. In addition, the Three Gorges of the Yangtze River can be used for hydroelectric power generation, providing a large amount of renewable energy, reducing coal consumption, and alleviating the air pollution problem along the Yangtze River.

The Three Gorges Dam project can meet the requirements of flood control, power generation, shipping, etc. At the same time, its impact on the ecological environment cannot be ignored. For example, due to the construction of the Three Gorges Reservoir, the submerged upland area is 632 square kilometers, and the directly submerged population is 846,200 people. In addition, 108 historical sites and cultural relics have been discovered in the Three Gorges Reservoir area, and some cultural relics will be destroyed due to the water storage of the Three Gorges Reservoir. Completely submerged or partially submerged, the more famous ones are Zhang Feimiao and Qu Yuantong. In addition, the cost of building a reservoir is extremely high, and the reservoir will silt up after years, which will reduce the flood control capacity of the reservoir.

It can be seen that the Three Gorges Dam project has both advantages and disadvantages.

        ).end_scores.squeeze(dim=-1)
        return {
            'eval/reward': reward_score,
        }

    def compute_kl_divergence(
        self,
        prompt: torch.LongTensor,  # size = (B, S) # pylint: disable=unused-argument
        log_probs: torch.Tensor,  # size = (B, L)
        ref_log_probs: torch.Tensor,  # size = (B, L)
        reward_score: torch.Tensor,  # size = (B,)
        sequence_mask: torch.BoolTensor,  # size = (B, L)
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        kl_divergence_estimate = -self.kl_coeff * (log_probs - ref_log_probs)  # size = (B, L)
        rewards = kl_divergence_estimate  # size = (B, L)
        reward_clip = torch.clamp(  # size = (B,)
            reward_score,
            min=-self.clip_range_score,
            max=self.clip_range_score,
        )
        batch_size = log_probs.size(0)
        for i in range(batch_size):
            end_index = sequence_mask[i].nonzero()[-1]
            rewards[i, end_index] += reward_clip[i]

        return rewards

    def actor_loss_fn(
        self,
        log_probs: torch.Tensor,
        old_log_probs: torch.Tensor,
        advantages: torch.Tensor,
        mask: torch.BoolTensor,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        # policy gradient loss
        ratio = torch.exp(log_probs - old_log_probs)
        pg_loss1 = -advantages * ratio
        pg_loss2 = -advantages * torch.clamp(
            ratio,
            1.0 - self.clip_range_ratio,
            1.0 + self.clip_range_ratio,
        )
        return torch.sum(torch.maximum(pg_loss1, pg_loss2) * mask) / mask.sum()

        attention_mask = rl_batch['attention_mask']

        start = prompt.size(-1) - 1
        sequence_mask = attention_mask[:, 1:]

        with torch.no_grad():
            old_rewards = self.compute_kl_divergence(
                prompt,
                old_log_probs,
                ref_log_probs,
                rewards,
                sequence_mask,
            )
            reward_advantages, reward_returns = self.get_advantages_and_returns(
                old_reward_values,
                old_rewards,
                start,
            )

        logits = self.actor_model(input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask, use_cache=False).logits
        log_prob = gather_log_probabilities(logits[:, :-1], input_ids[:, 1:])
        actor_loss = self.actor_loss_fn(
            log_prob[:, start:],
            old_log_probs[:, start:],
            reward_advantages,
            sequence_mask[:, start:],
        )
        self.actor_model.backward(actor_loss)
        self.actor_model.step()

        reward_values = self.reward_critic_model(
            input_ids,
            attention_mask=attention_mask,
            use_cache=False,

        reward_values = reward_values.squeeze(dim=-1)[:, :-1]
        reward_critic_loss = self.critic_loss_fn(

            old_reward_values[:, start:],
            reward_returns,
            sequence_mask[:, start:],
        )
        self.reward_critic_model.backward(reward_critic_loss)
        self.reward_critic_model.step()

        with torch.no_grad():
            kl_divergence = (
                ((old_log_probs - ref_log_probs) * sequence_mask)[:, start:].sum(dim=-1).mean()
            )

        rewards = rewards.mean()
        if dist.is_initialized():
            dist.reduce(actor_loss, dst=0, op=dist.ReduceOp.AVG)
            dist.reduce(reward_critic_loss, dst=0, op=dist.ReduceOp.AVG)
            dist.reduce(rewards, dst=0, op=dist.ReduceOp.AVG)

        dist.barrier()

        return {

            'train/reward_critic_loss': reward_critic_loss.item(),
            'train/reward': rewards.item(),
            'train/kl_divergence': kl_divergence.item(),

array_agg(DISTINCT tasks_exams.exam_id) AS exams_id,
array_agg(DISTINCT classes.name) AS class_name,

INNER JOIN tasks_authors

INNER JOIN tasks_classes

INNER JOIN exams

When I used to think of inventors, I pictured old men with grey beards. I pictured white lab coats and smoky beakers. I was surprised to learn that young people have created many world-changing inventions. 

Like 15-year old Albert Sadacca, who invented Christmas tree lights. The year was 1917. The place was New York city. Someone was hanging candles from a Christmas tree, as was common at that time. This started a tragic fire. Sadacca's parents sold electric lighting in their shop. Young Albert thought to adapt these lights for use on Christmas trees. This turned out to be a pretty bright idea. 

Another 12-year old visionary was Louis Braille. Braille was blind in both eyes.  In 1819 young Louis was attending one of the world's first schools for blind children. He learned a system of touch-based literacy, but it was hard for him to write. Braille sought a better way to communicate with his classmates. He wanted to write freely, without needing special equipment. So he taught himself a system of night-writing used in the military. Then he made a few changes to it. By the time he turned 15, he had created Braille. People with visual impairments today still use Braille to read and write.

Another cool kid who changed the world was 11-year old Frank Epperson. Frank was chilling on his porch one night in 1905. He went to bed and forgot his cup of lemonade on the porch. When he woke the next morning, young Frank realized that he had created the world's first Popsicle. He would later patent the concept and trademark the name "Popsicle." Frank's idea was so successful that many people still call ANY frozen treat a Popsicle.
Speaking of cool kids, 15-year old Chester Greenwood was ice-skating one day in 1873. Naturally, as tends to happen during winter play, his ears got cold. Chester had a clever idea. He asked his grandma to sew some fur tufts to a wire loop that he had fashioned. His design worked well! He had invented earmuffs. He patented his "ear protectors" as he called them. They were manufactured in his hometown of Farmington, Maine. Greenwood's one good idea provided jobs for people in the Farmington area for 60 years. 



Margaret E. Knight is another young person who became a small town hero. She is best remembered as the woman who invented the flat-bottomed paper bag. But she made her first life-saving device at the age of 12. Her brothers were working at a textile mill in town. One day she was visiting them. A loom malfunctioned and injured a worker. She thought she could make the machines safer. She invented an effective system. Her method was later used in many factories. She saved a lot of lives. And we still use the paper bag design that she created in 1868. How many lives have those saved? Am I right?



Some young people feel powerless. They feel like they are living in an adult world, created by adults for adults. But the truth is that everyone has the power to change the world. A 12 year-old girl growing up in 1868 made factories safer. A 15 year-old boy, blind in both eyes, made written communication more accessible. An 11 year-old forgot to put away his drink and it froze. Who knows what's in store for your future?

“What do you mean?”

“You know…”

“You remember him.”

“I remember me.”

“That makes you him.”

“Uh-huh,” she murmured sleepily.

The sharp-faced man looked offended for a brief second, then slipped into a placatory smile. “I’m afraid there’s been a misunderstanding, my good man. We’ve come for a room.”

The clerk looked them over again. The Langham had a certain standard of clientele. Royalty. Nobility. Artistes. A standard this pair, even should they have the money, most certainly did not approach.

“I know how it looks,” the man sighed, exhaustion in every syllable. “We were waylaid coming up from the docks. They took everything—everything,” Spike intoned, enjoying every minute of his performance. “We were rescued by one of God’s own saints, who lent us these clothes. We’re eager to rest, as you might imagine.”

“Awful luck,” the clerk commented neutrally.

“Indeed,” Spike continued, like some demented thespian. “Not the welcome to this fair city I was hoping for for my bride.”

Buffy’s shock at Spike’s alibi must have passed for shock at the situation as a whole, and the clerk’s expression softened.

“Quite terrible,” he clucked. “But I'm afraid we cannot give rooms on credit…”

“Not a problem,” Spike said smoothly. “We can pay now.”

The clerk raised his eyebrows. “You have the money on you, sir?”

Spike’s face went blank for a moment. Oops. He floundered for a reason why thieves would leave them their money. “Just our traveling funds. The thieves didn’t search us that closely, thank the good Lord.”

Buffy’s face twitched, and the clerk took it for embarrassment. His wife had been known to secret coins in some fairly intimate places in her clothing. The young missus must have done the same. And if their traveling funds alone could buy lodging… well, it’d be easy enough to expel them later, should their story unravel.

“The Langham would be glad to assist you in this time of distress, sir. The room will be six pounds for tonight. Meals are served regularly in our world-renowned dining room. Do come see me or any of our staff if you require anything.” Spike passed over a suspicious mix of coins and bills while the clerk gave his spiel, and they disappeared into the drawer alongside the revolver. The clerk turned briefly to pull a key down from the rack behind him.

“Room 203,” he chirped. “Not quite our honeymoon suite, but lovely accommodations nonetheless.” He shot a smile at Buffy that put Spike’s teeth on edge.

“Thanks, mate,” he responded, letting an edge of his rougher accent seep through. The clerk gaped, but Spike had already steered Buffy away, his hand on her back.

Buffy stumbled a bit as they headed up the stairs, the carpet lush under her aching feet. Spike worked the heavy iron key into the door, and with little fanfare she headed for the bed and toppled into it headfirst. Spike shut the door behind them, noted that the curtains were pulled shut, and realized that there was no way to get in the bed with her the way she’d fallen slantways across it.

He was so tired he almost didn’t care. Being with the slayer full-time was bloody exhilarating until it was bloody exhausting.

There was a little sofa with large decorative cushions to the side of the room. He pulled them off and tossed them on the floor next to the bed. He threw off his hat and coat, wrestled off his boots, and curled up by the bedskirt. He wasn’t in bed with Buffy, but he was closer, and that was something.

From above him came a voice so tired and small and mumbling that it took his vampire hearing to suss out the words:

“Hey Spike… remind me to be mad at you in the morning.”
